overview: Botswana is a landlocked country in southern Africa. Its capital and largest city is Gaborone. Botswana became independent from the United Kingdom in 1966 and has been one of Africa's most stable democracies. It is one of the world's largest producers of diamonds, which helped it grow quickly.

geography.text: About 70 percent of Botswana is covered by the Kalahari Desert, a dry, sandy savanna. In the north-west, the Okavango river spreads out into the Okavango Delta, a huge inland delta that floods every year and draws enormous numbers of animals. The Makgadikgadi Pans in the north-east are among the largest salt flats in the world.

history.text: Tswana chiefdoms lived in the region when, in 1885, Britain made it the protectorate of Bechuanaland, partly to stop it being taken over by South Africa. Botswana became independent in 1966 as one of the poorest countries in the world. Diamonds were found the next year, and careful use of that wealth made it one of Africa's most stable and prosperous democracies.

events.title: Chiefs go to London
events.text: Three chiefs travel to Britain to stop their land being handed to a mining company.

events.title: Independence
events.text: Botswana becomes independent under Seretse Khama.

government.text: Botswana is a parliamentary republic in which parliament elects the President, who is head of state and government. It has held free elections since independence in 1966. In 2024 the governing party lost power for the first time, and the change of government was peaceful.

economy.text: Diamonds turned Botswana from one of the poorest countries in the world into an upper-middle-income country. It is one of the world's largest producers of diamonds by value. Beef and tourism are also important.

culture.text: Botswana is home to the Okavango Delta, a vast inland wetland teeming with wildlife, and the Kalahari Desert. It has the largest elephant population in the world. The San people have lived in the Kalahari for tens of thousands of years.

items.title: Okavango Delta
items.text: A river delta that floods the desert every year, listed by UNESCO.

items.title: Elephants
items.text: About 130,000 elephants, the most of any country.

items.title: Tsodilo Hills
items.text: Rock art sacred to the San.

sport.text: Football is the most popular sport. In 2024 sprinter Letsile Tebogo won the Olympic 200 m, Botswana's first gold medal, and its men's relay team won silver.

items.text: Letsile Tebogo won Olympic gold in the 200 m.

items.title: Nijel Amos
items.text: Won 800 m silver at the 2012 Olympics.

didYouKnow: Botswana has more elephants than any other country, about 130,000.
The Okavango is a river delta that floods into the desert instead of the sea.
